title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on the Implementation of Sino-Foreign Judicial Assistance Agreements
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on the Implementation of Agreements on Judicial Assistance with Foreign Countries

Fa (Ban) Fa [1988] No. 3

To: All Higher People's Courts of Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly under the Central Government; All Intermediate People's Courts, Railway Transport Intermediate Courts, and Maritime Courts:

Since China adopted the policy of opening to the outside world, many countries have successively requested to conclude agreements on judicial assistance with China. Last year, China concluded agreements on judicial assistance with France, Poland, and Belgium respectively. Among them, the Agreement between the People's Republic of China and the Polish People's Republic on Judicial Assistance in Civil and Criminal Matters (see appendix) has already exchanged instruments of ratification and will enter into force on February 13, 1988. This Agreement is hereby transmitted to you for study and implementation.

In the future, some more countries will conclude agreements on judicial assistance with China. For the correct implementation of the agreements on judicial assistance concluded between China and foreign countries, notice is hereby given as follows:

1. Where a foreign contracting party submits a request for judicial assistance and the attached documents to a Chinese court through the Ministry of Justice of China, after the Ministry of Justice transmits them to this Court, this Court shall review them and forward them to the relevant higher people's court, which shall designate the relevant intermediate people's court or special court to handle the matter. The court executing the request must handle it carefully and responsibly in strict accordance with the content of the agreement on judicial assistance concluded with that country. After completion, the matter shall be reported to the original higher people's court for review and then forwarded to this Court. This Court shall review the matter, translate it into a foreign language, and together with the original documents, transmit them to the Ministry of Justice, which shall then forward them to the foreign contracting party that made the request.

2. Where a Chinese court requires judicial assistance from a court of a foreign contracting party, it must also submit a request and the attached documents in accordance with the provisions of the agreement on judicial assistance with that country. After review by the higher people's court to which it is subordinate, the matter shall be forwarded to this Court. This Court shall review the matter, translate it into a foreign language, and together with the Chinese request and attached documents, transmit them to the Ministry of Justice, which shall then forward them to the foreign contracting party.

3. If China and a country with which it has not yet concluded an agreement on judicial assistance mutually require judicial assistance, the matter shall still be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation) and the provisions of the Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Ministry of Justice of August 14, 1986, on Several Questions Concerning the Mutual Commissioning of Service of Legal Documents through Diplomatic Channels between Chinese Courts and Foreign Courts.

Appendix: Agreement between the People's Republic of China and the Polish People's Republic on Judicial Assistance in Civil and Criminal Matters.

February 1, 1988

Agreement between the People's Republic of China and the Polish People's Republic on Judicial Assistance in Civil and Criminal Matters

The People's Republic of China and the Polish People's Republic, on the basis of respect for national sovereignty, independence, equality, and mutual benefit, and for the purpose of strengthening friendly relations of cooperation in the judicial field, have decided to conclude this Agreement. To this end, the following provisions have been agreed upon:

Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 Judicial Protection

Nationals of one Contracting Party shall, in the territory of the other Contracting Party, enjoy the same judicial protection as nationals of the other Contracting Party and shall have the right to institute proceedings or make requests in the courts or other authorities of the other Contracting Party under the same conditions as nationals of the other Contracting Party.

Article 2 Exemption from Security for Costs

The courts and other authorities competent in civil cases of one Contracting Party shall not require nationals of the other Contracting Party who have their domicile or residence in the territory of the other Contracting Party to provide security for costs in civil proceedings.

Article 3 Advance Payment of Costs

Nationals of one Contracting Party shall, in the territory of the other Contracting Party, pay in advance civil procedure costs under the same conditions and to the same extent as nationals of the other Contracting Party.

Article 4 Legal Persons

The provisions of the preceding three articles shall also apply to legal persons.

Article 5 Reduction or Exemption of Costs

Nationals of one Contracting Party may, in the territory of the other Contracting Party, apply for a reduction or exemption of civil procedure costs under the same conditions and to the same extent as nationals of the other Contracting Party. An application by a national of one Contracting Party for reduction or exemption of civil procedure costs shall be supported by a certificate issued by the competent authority of the place of his domicile or residence; if the applicant has no domicile or residence in the territory of either Contracting Party, the certificate may be issued by a diplomatic or consular authority of his country.

Article 6 Channels for Judicial Assistance

1. The courts and other authorities of the two Contracting Parties shall provide judicial assistance to each other through direct communication between the central authorities of the two Contracting Parties.
2. The central authorities referred to in the preceding paragraph shall be designated by the two Contracting Parties through diplomatic channels.

Article 7 Requests for Judicial Assistance

1. A request for judicial assistance shall be made in the form of a letter of request. The letter of request for judicial assistance shall contain the following: the name of the requesting and requested authorities, the names, nationalities, occupations, domiciles or residences of the parties, the name and address of the representative, and the specific subject matter of the request for judicial assistance. Other documents and information necessary for the execution of the request shall also be provided with the letter of request.
2. A request for judicial assistance in criminal matters shall be accompanied by a description of the facts of the crime to which the request relates and the relevant legal provisions.
3. The said letters of request and documents shall be signed and sealed by the requesting authority of one Contracting Party.

Article 8 Language

Correspondence and documents transmitted within the scope of judicial assistance shall be written in the national language of one Contracting Party and accompanied by a translation into the language of the other Contracting Party or into English.

Article 9 Costs of Judicial Assistance

1. The two Contracting Parties shall provide judicial assistance to each other free of charge.
2. Travel and accommodation expenses of witnesses or experts summoned to appear in the territory of the requesting Contracting Party shall be borne by the requesting Contracting Party. Upon the request of the person concerned, the competent authority of the requesting Contracting Party shall advance the said expenses.

Article 10 Refusal of Judicial Assistance

If the requested Contracting Party considers that the provision of judicial assistance would impair its sovereignty, security, or public order, it may refuse to provide judicial assistance, but shall notify the requesting Contracting Party of the reasons for the refusal.

Article 11 Law Applicable to Judicial Assistance

1. In providing judicial assistance, the requested authority shall apply its own national law.
2. In providing civil judicial assistance, the requested authority may, upon request, also apply the law of the other Contracting Party, provided that this does not contravene the fundamental principles of the law of the requested Contracting Party.

Article 12 Definitions

The term "civil cases" as used in this Agreement also includes cases concerning property rights and personal rights within the scope of commercial law, marriage law, labour law, and the like.

Chapter II Service of Documents and Taking of Evidence in Civil Matters

Article 13 Scope

The two Contracting Parties shall, upon request, mutually serve judicial documents and extrajudicial documents, interrogate parties, witnesses, and experts, conduct expert evaluations and judicial inspections, and collect other evidence.

Article 14 Execution of Requests

1. If the authority of the requested Contracting Party considers itself incompetent to execute the request, it shall transmit the request to the competent authority with the power to execute it and shall notify the requesting authority.
2. If the authority of the requested Contracting Party is unable to execute the request in accordance with the address indicated in the letter of request, it shall take appropriate measures to ascertain the correct address and complete the requested act; if necessary, it may request the requesting Contracting Party to provide additional information.
3. If, due to the inability to ascertain the address or for other reasons, the request cannot be executed, the authority of the requested Contracting Party shall notify the requesting Contracting Party, specifying the specific reasons, and shall return the documents attached by the requesting Contracting Party.

Article 15 Notification of Execution

1. The competent authority of the requested Contracting Party shall, through the channel provided for in Article 6, paragraph 1 of this Agreement, notify the competent authority of the requesting Contracting Party of the date and place of execution of the service of documents or taking of evidence, and shall attach the certificate of service or the evidentiary materials obtained.
2. The certificate of service shall indicate the date of receipt and the signature of the addressee, and the seal and signature of the serving authority and the server. If the addressee refuses to accept the document, the reason for the refusal shall be noted.

Chapter III Recognition and Enforcement of Civil Judgments

Article 16 Scope

1. The two Contracting Parties shall, under the conditions provided for in this Agreement, recognize or enforce in their respective territories the following judgments rendered in the territory of the other Contracting Party after the entry into force of this Agreement:
   (1) judgments rendered by courts in civil cases;
   (2) judgments rendered by courts in criminal cases relating to claims for compensation;
   (3) judgments rendered by competent authorities in inheritance cases;
   (4) awards rendered by arbitral tribunals.
2. The term "judgments" as used in this Agreement also includes mediation agreements.

Article 17 Documents to Be Attached to the Request

A request for recognition and enforcement of a judgment shall be accompanied by the following documents:
(1) a copy of the judgment certified to be in conformity with the original. If the copy does not expressly state that the judgment has become final and is enforceable, it shall be accompanied by a document issued by the court certifying that it has become final and is enforceable;
(2) the certificate of service or other documents proving that the judgment has been served;
(3) a document issued by the court certifying that the losing party has been duly summoned and, where lacking procedural capacity, has been properly represented;
(4) a translation of the letter of request and the documents referred to in the preceding three items into the language of the requested Contracting Party or into English, certified to be correct.

Article 18 Procedure for Recognition and Enforcement

1. A request for recognition or enforcement of a judgment may be submitted by a court of one Contracting Party to a court of the other Contracting Party through the channel provided for in Article 6, paragraph 1 of this Agreement, or may be submitted directly by a party to the court of the other Contracting Party having jurisdiction over the recognition or enforcement.
2. In the procedure for recognition and enforcement of a judgment, the court shall only examine whether the judgment meets the conditions provided for in this Agreement.

Article 19 Effect of Recognition and Enforcement

A judgment of one Contracting Party, once recognized or enforced by a court of the other Contracting Party, shall have the same effect as a judgment rendered by the court that recognizes or enforces it.

Article 20 Refusal of Recognition and Enforcement

A judgment enumerated in Article 16 of this Agreement shall not be recognized or enforced in any of the following circumstances:
(1) the judgment was rendered by a court without jurisdiction according to the law of the Contracting Party in which recognition or enforcement is sought;
(2) the judgment has not become final or is not enforceable according to the law of the Contracting Party in which it was rendered;
(3) the losing party was not duly summoned by a court according to the law of the Contracting Party in which the judgment was rendered;
(4) the party was deprived of the possibility to defend itself, or, where lacking procedural capacity, was deprived of proper representation;
(5) a court of the Contracting Party in which recognition or enforcement is sought has rendered a final judgment on a case between the same parties on the same subject matter, or is already hearing such a case, or has already recognized a final judgment rendered by a court of a third country on the same case;
(6) recognition or enforcement of the judgment would impair the fundamental principles of law or public order of the Contracting Party in which recognition or enforcement is sought.

Article 21 Recognition and Enforcement of Arbitral Awards

The two Contracting Parties shall, in accordance with the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards signed in New York on June 10, 1958, mutually recognize and enforce arbitral awards made in the territory of the other Contracting Party.

Chapter IV Service of Documents and Taking of Evidence in Criminal Matters

Article 22 Scope

The two Contracting Parties shall, upon request, mutually serve judicial documents and extrajudicial documents in criminal matters, hear statements of parties and suspects, interrogate witnesses, victims, and experts, conduct expert evaluations, inspections, and judicial examinations, and collect other evidence.

Article 23 Execution of Requests and Notification of Execution

The provisions of Articles 14 and 15 of this Agreement shall also apply to the service of documents and taking of evidence in criminal matters.

Article 24 Refusal of Criminal Judicial Assistance

The requested Contracting Party may refuse to provide criminal judicial assistance on any of the following grounds:
(1) if the requested Contracting Party considers that the crime to which the request relates is of a political nature or is a military offence;
(2) if, according to the law of the requested Contracting Party, the act to which the request relates does not constitute a crime;
(3) if the suspect or offender to whom the request relates is a national of the requested Contracting Party and is not within the territory of the requesting Contracting Party.

Article 25 Notification of Results of Criminal Proceedings

The two Contracting Parties shall transmit to each other copies of final judgments or summaries of cases rendered by their respective courts against nationals of the other Contracting Party.

Chapter V Other Provisions

Article 26 Exchange of Legal Information

The two Contracting Parties shall, upon request and through the channel provided for in Article 6, paragraph 1 of this Agreement, mutually provide information on their respective laws and judicial practices and exchange legal publications.

Article 27 Exemption from Authentication

Documents made or certified by a court or other competent authority of one Contracting Party and bearing its seal shall be used in the territory of the other Contracting Party without authentication.

Article 28 Protection of Witnesses and Experts

1. A witness or expert summoned to appear through notification by the requested Contracting Party shall not, regardless of his nationality, be prosecuted criminally or deprived of his liberty in any form by the requesting Contracting Party for any offence committed before his entry into its territory, or for his testimony, expert opinion, or any other act relating to the content of the proceedings.
2. If a witness or expert, having the possibility to leave the territory of the requesting Contracting Party, fails to do so within 15 days from the day following the notification that his presence is no longer required, he shall lose the protection granted under the preceding paragraph.

Article 29 Implementation of the Agreement

Any difficulties arising in the course of the implementation of this Agreement shall be resolved through diplomatic channels.

Chapter VI Final Provisions

Article 30 Ratification and Entry into Force

This Agreement is subject to ratification. The instruments of ratification shall be exchanged in Beijing. This Agreement shall enter into force on the thirtieth day after the date of exchange of instruments of ratification.

Article 31 Termination

Either Contracting Party may terminate this Agreement by written notification to the other Party. This Agreement shall cease to be effective twelve months after the date of the notice of termination; otherwise, this Agreement shall remain in force permanently.

Done in Warsaw on June 5, 1987, in two copies, each in the Chinese and Polish languages, both texts being equally authentic.

In witness whereof, the plenipotentiaries of the two Contracting Parties have signed and sealed this Agreement.

For the People's Republic of China: Qian Qichen
For the Polish People's Republic: Jan Majewski
